If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (8–14 days), reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (15–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (15–30 days) to prevent premature correction.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67) in the last 5 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing adjustment across all horizons to dampen erratic forecast swings.
